target.statement: Branch-and-bound explores far fewer full assignments than brute force on random partition graphs (e.g., the number of full assignments evaluated for R=2 at graph size n=26, log-scale value in Figure 1 left)
target.dataset: Synthetic random partition graphs from networkx (edge probs 0.01 within / 0.1 between, R=2, n up to 26)

compute.basis: No code released; the algorithm is fully specified in Algorithms 1-3 and data is generated by networkx, so an agent must reimplement branch-and-bound plus brute force and average over 50 repetitions of small graphs (n<=26, R=2), which is CPU-only and modest.

blockers: No code or configs released; algorithms must be reimplemented from pseudocode
Exact numeric values are only in figures (no table), so matching the plotted cell requires digitizing
Brute force at n=26, R=2 is 2^26 assignments per graph x 50 reps, which is heavy but feasible on CPU
title: Exact computation of the network modularity with branch-and-bound
